newsitem.title: JAPAN: Aramco naphtha talks to start on May 12 in S'pore.
newsitem.headline: Aramco naphtha talks to start on May 12 in S'pore.

text.p: Saudi Arabia has notified its potential naphtha lifters that negotiations for term cargoes to be loaded in the second half of 1997 will be held in Singapore in the third week of May, traders said on Friday.
Some participants in the first round of bidding, which closed on April 4, were screened out and not invited to the meeting because their bidding levels were not competitive, traders said.
The highest bid for A-180, paraffinic naphtha favoured as petrochemical feedstock, was believed to be around $15.00 over the Aramco formula, compared with a $6.50 premium for the first half of 1997.

Term premiums for Middle Eastern cargoes have risen sharply in the past year as the long-term supply and demand balance in Asia is expected to remain tight with new petrochemical plants springing up in the region.
In Singapore, state-owned oil firm Saudi Aramco is expected to have one-on-one talks with each potential buyer to exchange their views on market trends.
Aramco will also notify the potential term lifters of its offer price, traders said.
The supplier is expected to announce detailed schedule for the Singapore meeting early next week, they said.
Asian firms usually import about 4.5 million tonnes of term naphtha per year from Saudi Aramco, they added.
